name: Gie bo
summary: A Bahnar beef broth from the An Khê and Vĩnh Thạnh highlands, now eaten in Tây Sơn, made with fresh small intestine and soured with lá giang. Chili, ginger, and lemongrass go in, and a few drops of bile add the bitterness locals look for.
origin: Phú Phong, Tây Sơn. The dish is Bahnar, from An Khê and Vĩnh Thạnh.
taste: Chili, ginger, and lemongrass, sour lá giang, and a slight bitterness when a few drops of bile are added. That bitterness is the local taste.
howToEat: The bowl comes with fresh noodles, herbs, and toasted sesame rice paper. The broth is brown with a little green.
seoTitle: Gie bo — the Tay Son beef broth
seoDescription: Gié bò is a Bahnar beef broth now eaten in Tây Sơn, soured with lá giang, with noodles, herbs, and toasted sesame rice paper.
